READ passages: PDF p.4 definitions -- 'The Weak Energy Condition (WEC) T_ab u^a u^b >= 0 for all timelike u^a ... The Null Energy Condition (NEC) T_ab u^a u^b >= 0 for all null u^a ... The Dominant Energy Condition (DEC) T_ab u^a v^b >= 0 for all future-pointing timelike u^a and v^b. Interpretation: All observers see a causal flux of energy-momentum ... (SEC) T_ab u^a u^b - 1/2 g_ab T^ab >= 0'; PDF p.6 (Examples, after the scalar field's sum-of-squares WEC proof) -- 'Likewise, DEC also holds for this reason, and the same is true for the electromagnetic field.'; PDF p.1 abstract -- 'Quantum field theory violates all the classical energy conditions of general relativity'; PDF p.9 (Casimir) -- EM T_mu_nu = C(z)/L^4 diag(-1,1,1,-3), C_0 = pi^2/720 between plates, 'we have deduced that WEC is violated ... a choice of either accepting violations of the WEC or abandoning the standard electromagnetic stress-tensor based a conformally invariant Lagrangian', and 'there is no possibility of insisting on pointwise energy conditions in QFT'.

published_statement: Energy conditions (Fewster 1208.5399 p.4, restating Hawking-Ellis): WEC T_ab u^a u^b >= 0 for all timelike u; NEC the same for all null u; DEC T_ab u^a v^b >= 0 for all future-pointing timelike u, v (causal energy-momentum flux); SEC T_ab u^a u^b - (1/2) T g_ab u^a u^b >= 0. The classical electromagnetic field obeys WEC and DEC (p.6: 'DEC also holds ... and the same is true for the electromagnetic field'); NEC follows. The same source records that the QUANTIZED electromagnetic field violates WEC between Casimir plates (p.9) and that QFT violates all the classical pointwise energy conditions (abstract).
published_hypotheses: H1 classical field: T_ab is the classical Maxwell tensor F_ac F_b^c - (1/4) g_ab F^2 (Fewster p.6 is in the classical-field examples; p.1/p.9 state the quantized field violates WEC)
H2 linear (Maxwell) Lagrangian -F; the Casimir argument (p.9) turns on the conformally invariant (traceless) EM stress tensor
H3 the conditions are pointwise statements about the EM stress-energy ALONE -- the sources/confining matter of the field are a separate T_ab

H4 (definitional) WEC/NEC/DEC as stated for arbitrary T_ab; the eigenvalue forms rho>=0, rho+p_i>=0, rho>=|p_i| hold for Hawking-Ellis type I only (standard; not quoted in the read restatement, re-derived here by z3 for WEC/NEC and numerically for DEC)

The external result says nothing about stellar matter; the lens interior's |p| <= rho c^2 is not checked by any owner cited here (dimensional scale G M^2/R^4 / (mean rho c^2) = 8.9e-6 for the tree's M, R -- indicative only, not a solar model). The corridor itself is vacuum (T_ab = 0), which satisfies every condition trivially.

At the tree's 1e11 T the magnetic pressure is 3.9789e27 Pa (tree prints 3.979e27, reproduced), mass-equivalent 4.427e10 kg/m^3; DEC for a confining material requires its tension <= its energy density, a condition the EM result does not supply. NARROWED CHECK, NOT A PHYSICS ERROR -- charge.py:155-162 em_is_ordinary() hard-codes rho = 1.0, p_r = -rho, p_t = +rho and so returns True unconditionally: spec.py:305's chk cannot fail. Re-derived here that this is WLOG for every NON-NULL field (eigenvalues of T^a_b are {-L,-L,+L,+L}; conditions homogeneous in rho), but it omits the NULL (Hawking-Ellis type II) field; the null field is shown here to satisfy the conditions too, so the omission moves nothing. charge.py's WEC/NEC/DEC algebraic forms agree with the read definitions (z3 unsat on the negated equivalence for WEC and NEC; DEC numerically).

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/em-stress-energy-energy-conditions.out). A (sympy, exact, every F_ab): T_00=(E^2+B^2)/2, |T_0i|=|ExB|, trace 0, and the identity T_00^2 - |T_0i|^2 = ((E^2-B^2)^2+4(E.B)^2)/4 >= 0 -- since it holds for all E,B it holds in every observer's frame, so energy density >= 0 and the flux is causal: WEC and DEC for every classical Maxwell field, NEC by limit; 12,000 random (F,u,v) give T_ab u^a v^b >= 0. Characteristic polynomial of T^a_b = (lam^2 - L^2)^2: canonical frame (rho, -rho, +rho, +rho) = em_is_ordinary's eigenstructure; null field is nilpotent type II and passes NEC on 2,000 random null k. A6 (z3): 'T_ab u^a u^b >= 0 for all timelike/null u' <=> charge.py's algebraic WEC/NEC forms for type I (unsat on the negation; vacuity guard passes); DEC type-I form agrees with the flux definition on 300 random cases. B (sympy, general L(F)): T_ab k^a k^b = -L_F w.w with w.w = (E_x-B_y)^2+(E_y+B_x)^2 >= 0, so NEC <=> L_F <= 0; pure B: rho=-L, p_par=L, p_perp=L-B^2 L_F. C (numeric, mpmath; proper-time one-loop EH form NOT read at source, used only after it reproduced the weak-field coefficient to 0.99994 and the strong-field leading log e^2B^2/(24 pi^2) ln(eB/m^2) to 0.99942): at B/B_crit = 1, 22.65 (1e11 T), 226.5, 1e4, 1e8: L_F = -0.99993, -0.99877, -0.99716, -0.99425, -0.98712 (<0: NEC); rho/(B^2/2) = 0.99996..0.98751 (>0: WEC); DEC margin > 0. Leading-log NEC boundary at ln(B/B_crit) ~ 3 pi/alpha - 1/2 = 1291 (the Landau-pole scale). One bug in my own first draft (index placement in w.k) failed and was fixed before the recorded run.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The published result is a THEOREM about the classical Maxwell tensor; its conclusion uses no measured number, so no datum can move it -- re-derived here exactly for every F_ab (Part A). What the 1973 statement is silent on is its DOMAIN: (i) fields above B_crit = 4.414e9 T (magnetars at ~1e11 T were established after 1973 -- that observational history is not read here), where the linear Lagrangian is replaced by the QED effective one; (ii) quantum states, where pointwise conditions fail (Casimir, READ in Fewster p.9; the Casimir effect and QFT's pointwise violations were theoretically known before 1973, so this is not data the authors lacked). Evidence either way: for (i), within one-loop Euler-Heisenberg (form not read at source; internally consistent) NEC, WEC and DEC still hold at the tree's 1e11 T with L_F = -0.99877, and the leading-log sign change is at ln(B/B_crit) ~ 1291 -- so having the strong-field data does NOT change the conclusion for any field the tree names. For (ii), the conclusion does narrow, but by theory known at the time, and only for non-classical states/boundaries; the tree's use drops that hypothesis. Net: no evidence that the authors' data were inaccurate or incomplete in a way that moves this result.
grade_evidence: The external result itself is re-derived exactly and agrees: for EVERY classical Maxwell field, T_00 >= 0 and T_00^2 - |S|^2 = ((E^2-B^2)^2+4(E.B)^2)/4 >= 0 in every frame, so WEC, DEC and NEC hold (sympy identity + 12,000 numeric (F,u,v)); charge.py's energy-condition definitions agree with the read definitions (z3). Nothing in it is WRONG, and no datum moves it. The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than it covers: (1) spec.py:190 DOES[1] and specthm SR1 claim NEC/WEC/DEC 'everywhere' for a positive-MASS lens, and the only check cited, spec.py:305 -> charge.em_is_ordinary() (charge.py:155-162, a constant that returns True unconditionally), is about EM stress-energy, not lens matter; (2) the tree drops 'classical field' (the read source itself records WEC violation by the quantized EM field, p.9) and (3) 'EM stress-energy alone' (spec.py:99-101's 'everywhere' for a sustained field includes confining matter at 3.98e27 Pa). The drop of 'linear Maxwell' at 22.7 B_crit was computed not to move the conclusion within one-loop QED (conditional on an unread EH form). The narrowing is of the tree's USE; the tree's lensing conclusion is not shown false -- it is shown unsupported by this particular check.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: an owner that (a) states 'classical field' and 'EM stress-energy alone' as hypotheses where it cites the result, and (b) checks the lens-matter conditions for SR1/DOES[1] separately (e.g. a stellar-model |p| <= rho c^2 check read at source), with em_is_ordinary computing T from a field rather than returning a constant. To WRONG: only a computed classical Maxwell field with T_ab u^a v^b < 0 -- ruled out by the Part A identity. Part C's QED sub-claim would move to OPEN/contested if the one-loop EH form, once READ at source (hep-th/0406216), differs from the form used; if two-loop or nonperturbative terms flipped L_F below the Landau-pole scale (not expected, not checked), the linear-Maxwell drop would become load-bearing.
